title: Je suis bien ici  (I'm Fine Here)

segments.t: What nobody here knows is that Mathias is her father. Now he walks down the corridor and finds her, at work, in his own agency. Later, his assistant Noémie, who has seen them argue, has a word with Camille. First the whole scene in French. Don't worry about catching every word. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
J'ai trouvé un travail. Super, non?
Un travail?
Je suis la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa Martel.
Écoute, j'ai mal réagi ce matin.
Je ne m'attendais pas à te voir.
Si tu veux, je peux t'aider à trouver un poste.
C'est gentil, mais je suis bien ici.
Non, Camille! Ce n'est pas possible.
Pourquoi?
Parce que tu ne peux pas. C'est ma vie!
Tu ne me donnes rien.
Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!
Bonjour. En fait, vous et lui...
Mathias, vous savez, est marié.
Il est très, très marié.
Let's take it slowly. Mathias stops dead when he sees Camille in the corridor, and his first words are not exactly a warm hello.
Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
'What are you doing here?' He uses the casual 'you', the one for family and friends, so we already sense these two know each other well. Camille answers brightly.
J'ai trouvé un travail.
'I found a job.' This is the past French uses most in conversation: a helper word, 'have', plus the action. Literally 'I have found a job'.
Super, non?
'Great, isn't it?' Adding the little word for 'no' with a question mark at the end is an easy way to ask for agreement. Mathias can only repeat her words.
Je suis la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa Martel.
'I'm Andréa Martel's new assistant.' The word for 'new' takes its feminine form, because Camille is a woman. And to say whose assistant she is, French puts the owner last, after a small linking word.
Écoute, j'ai mal réagi ce matin.
'Listen, I reacted badly this morning.' He starts with a casual command, 'listen', to calm things down. It's almost an apology.
Je ne m'attendais pas à te voir.
'I wasn't expecting to see you.' Notice how the negative wraps around the action word: one small word before it, and the word for 'not' after it. Then he makes an offer.
Si tu veux, je peux t'aider à trouver un poste.
'If you want, I can help you find a job.' He means anywhere else, a nice long way from his agency. Camille is polite, but she doesn't move an inch.
C'est gentil, mais je suis bien ici.
'That's kind, but I'm fine here.' Literally 'I am well here'. This is the line that makes Mathias lose his temper. In the show he swears; here we keep it clean.
Non, Camille! Ce n'est pas possible.
'No, Camille! It's not possible.' Here is that negative wrap again, around the verb 'is'. In fast speech the French often drop the first little word, and you'll hear exactly that in the episode.
Pourquoi?
'Why?' One short word, and Camille stands her ground.
Parce que tu ne peux pas.
'Because you can't.' The verb here means 'to be able to', and it often stands alone like this.
C'est ma vie!
'It's my life!' His job, his agency, his secret: he wants her out of all of it.
Tu ne me donnes rien.
'You give me nothing.' Another negative wrap, this time with a different second word, the one that means 'nothing'. Camille fires back.
Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!

'So I'll manage on my own, as always!' That verb in the middle is a very French one: to get by, to sort yourself out. The word for 'alone' is feminine here, because she is talking about herself. Then Mathias walks off.
Bonjour. En fait, vous et lui...
'Hello. Actually, you and him...' Noémie, Mathias's assistant, has heard everything, and she has completely misunderstood. She uses the polite 'you' with the newcomer.
Mathias, vous savez, est marié.
'Mathias, you know, is married.' She thinks Camille is a girlfriend, not a daughter.
Il est très, très marié.
'He's very, very married.' Saying a word twice is a fun way to make it stronger, and Camille can't tell her the truth.
Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
J'ai trouvé un travail. Super, non?
Un travail?
Je suis la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa Martel.
Écoute, j'ai mal réagi ce matin.
Je ne m'attendais pas à te voir.
Si tu veux, je peux t'aider à trouver un poste.
C'est gentil, mais je suis bien ici.
Non, Camille! Ce n'est pas possible.
Pourquoi?
Parce que tu ne peux pas. C'est ma vie!
Tu ne me donnes rien.
Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!
Bonjour. En fait, vous et lui...
Mathias, vous savez, est marié.
Il est très, très marié.
That's it for this scene, and you followed a real family row in French. When you watch it, listen for 'I'm fine here', and for Noémie's very married Mathias. See you next time!
À bientôt!
